Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel 
with Mr. Nishant Krishna Adhikari, learned

2. Mr. Narayan Dutt, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/

Government Standing Counsel for 
respondent Nos.2&3.
4. Petitioners who are working as T.G.T.
Teachers in the Eklavya Model Residential 
School have been relieved from their services,
as their contractual engagement has not 
been extended.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel 
for the petitioner that the respondents are 
bent upon to dispense with the services of 
the petitioners and earlier also, an attempt 
was made when online advertisement was 
issued in the month of July, 2023 by Central 
Society to fill up the vacancies on the post of 
teaching and non-teaching staff of the said 
EMR School.
6. The petitioners, feeling aggrieved, 
challenged the aforesaid advertisement, by 
filing writ petition Nos.1681 of 2023 (S/S) 
and 1414 of 2023(S/S) before this Court and 
this Court has been pleased to grant interim 
order by staying the selection process 
pursuant to the aforesaid advertisement. 2
7. Now, despite making a clear stand 
before a Division Bench of this Court in
Special Appeal Nos.331 of 2023 and 342 of 
2023 preferred against the interim order 
passed in aforesaid writ petitions, that the 
petitioners shall not be touched, but, the 
respondents have adopted another mode to 
throw away the petitioners from the Society 
and consequently, the impugned order dated 
30.05.2024 has been passed.
8. Learned counsel for the respondents 
pray for and are granted two weeks’ time to 
file counter affidavits.
9. Issue notice to respondent Nos.4 & 5.
10. Steps to be taken within 03 days.
11. List immediately after fresh cases on 
28.06.2024.

WPSS No.950/2024,

And
WPSS No.911/2024
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Ramji Shrivastava and Mr. Nishant Krishna Adhikari, 
learned counsel for the petitioners. 
2. Mr. Narayan Dutt, learned Standing Counsel for the State of 
Uttarkhand/ respondent no.1.
3. Mr. Manoj Kumar and Mr. Saurav Adhikari, learned Standing 
Counsel for the Union of India/respondent no.2.
4. Petitioners are the contractual employees of respondent no.5-
Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS), Jogla, P.O. Kalsi Gate, 
Kalsi, District Dehradun. An online advertisement was issued by 
respondent no.3/National Education Society for Tribal Students 
(NESTS) for supplying the vacancies of teaching and non-teaching 
staff of EMRS throughout India including EMRS in State of 
Uttarakhand. The petitioners are working with the respondent no.5/ 
Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for the last two to thirteen 
years and so. 
5. Feeling aggrieved with the online advertisement, some of the 
Teaching and Non-Teaching Staff of the EMRS moved to this Court 
by filing Writ Petition (S/S) Nos.1414, 1427, 1680 and 1681 of 2023. 
6. This Court after hearing both the parties reached to this 
conclusion that prima facie, respondent no.3-National Education 
Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) has got no legal right to notify 
the vacancies with regard to Eklavya Model Residential School 
(EMRS) in the State of Uttarakhand as per the new guidelines issued 
for EMRS. As per Clause 9.3(e) and (f) of the aforesaid new  2
guidelines, the power for recruitment of teaching and non-teaching 
staff of the schools was given to State Level Society i.e. EMRS 
Society-respondent no.3. Consequently, the selection process pursuant 
to the online advertisement was stayed by this Court vide interim 
orders dated 17.08.2023 and 12.09.2023 passed in those writ petitions. 
7. Feeling aggrieved by the interim orders passed by this Court, 
the respondent no.3-NESTS took these matters to the Division Bench 
of this Court by filing of Special Appeal Nos. 331, 334, 342 and 344 
of 2023. The aforesaid special appeals have been disposed of by the 
Division Bench on the basis of a concessional statement made by the 
appellant-NESTS therein along with the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, 
Government of India. The portion of the undertaking given by the 
appellant and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, quoted in the judgment 
and order of Division Bench is reproduced below…….
“The appellants filed their counter-affidavits, along with an 
application to seek vacation of the stay granted by this Court 
against the recruitment process. The stand taken by the 
appellants in their counter-affidavit, inter alia, is that the 
recruitment process in question, is not being made in respect 
of posts held by the respondents- writ petitioners. In 
Paragraph No.14 of the counter-affidavit, the stand taken by 
the appellants is as follows:-
“14. That the contents of para 25 of the writ petition 
to make the matter abundantly clear it is submitted that 
presently NESTS would not post any teacher against the 
posts occupied by these 28 contractual teachers in 
Uttarakhand. As of now, NESTS has not published the 
posts held by contractual teachers as they are engaged 
by state. The contract of teaches is with state society. 
NESTS has nothing to do with their continuation or 
discontinuation. However, our recruitment is being 
conducted in such a way as not to disturb the current 
contractual teachers”. 3
8. From the perusal of the undertaking given by the appellant￾NESTS and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Uttarakhand, it is revealed
beyond doubt that the recruitment process, which was in question, was 
not being made in respect of the post(s) held by the respondent￾petitioners in special appeals. Now, after having given such an
undertaking by filing the counter affidavit, respondent nos. 2 and 3 
have now turned around and they are in haste to fill up the vacancies 
held by the petitioners for the last so many years, though on 
contractual basis. 
9. Since it has been held by this Court while hearing the connected 
writ petitions filed by some of the petitioners that the central society
(NESTS) has got no right to issue an advertisement for supplying the 
vacancies in the Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS), the said 
exercise is totally illegal and bereft of any merit for the reason that 
since the very inception as per new guidelines, the advertisement 
cannot be issued by the Central Society. It is in the exclusive domain 
and competence of State Level Society i.e. respondent no.4
10. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that 
pursuant to the earlier impugned online advertisement, the selection 
process has been concluded and the respondents now are in haste of 
giving joining to the selected persons on the post held by the 
petitioners. 
11. Feeling aggrieved, the petitioners are before this Court. 
12. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents submits that the 
term of the petitioners has not been extended beyond 30.05.2024, and 
therefore, the petitioners have no right to continue.
13. Having considered the rival submissions made by learned 
counsel for the parties and having gone through the record of the writ 
petition, this Court is of the view that once the undertaking has been  4
given by the NESTS-respondent no.3 and Ministry of Tribal Affairs￾respondent no.2 before the Division Bench of this Court while 
deciding the special appeals that no selection process would be held 
for the post on which the petitioners are working, this exercise which 
is being done by respondents is illegal and contemptuous too.
14. Issue notice to respondent nos.3, 4 & 5, returnable within six 
weeks. 
15. Steps to be taken within one week. 
16. Respondents may file counter affidavit within six weeks. 
17. Rejoinder affidavit may file within two weeks thereafter. 
18. List these matters on 18.09.2024.
19. In the meantime, the respondents are restrained from giving 
joining to any of the persons selected on the post(s) as held by the 
petitioners in the respondent no.5-Institution.
20. Let a certified copy of this order be supplied to the learned 
counsel for the parties, today itself, as per rules. 
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)

1. Mr. Ramji Shrivastava, learned counsel 
along with Mr. Nishant Krishna Adhikari, learned 
counsel for the petitioners in WPSS Nos. 909/2024, 
911/2024 and 950/2024.
2. Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Senior 
Counsel assisted by Mr. Shubhang Dobhal, learned 
counsel for the petitioners in WPSS Nos. 1945/2024 
and 1946/2024.
3. Mr. Narayan Dutt, learned Brief Holder 
for the State/respondent No. 1.
4. Mr. Saurabh Adhikari, learned Standing 
Counsel along with Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned 
Standing Counsel for the Union of India/respondent 
No. 2.
5. Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned Senior 
Counsel, assisted by Mr. Y.C. Brijwasi and Mr. 
Abhishek Anthwal, learned counsels for 
NESTS/respondent No. 3.
6. Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned counsel for 
respondent Nos. 4 & 5.
7. In all these petitions issues are 
common. 
8. In Writ Petition (S/S) No. 920 of 2024, 
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 911 of 2024 and Writ 
Petition (S/S) No. 950 of 2024 the petitioners, who  were engaged on contractual basis in different 
Institutions, challenging the order dated 
30.05.2024 whereby their contractual 
appointments were discontinued. 
9. The coordinate Bench of this Court, by 
order dated 12.06.2024 restrained the respondents 
from giving joining to any of the persons selected 
through open selection on the post, held by the 
petitioners in the Institution.
10. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned 
counsel for the petitioners submits that the 
petitioners are challenging the order impugned 
dated 30.05.2024 on the ground that, in fact, 
against the posts occupied by these contractual 
employees, the regular selection has taken place 
though, Mr. Arvind Vashisth, the learned Senior 
Counsel, appearing for the National Education 
Society for Tribal Students (NESTS) gave an 
undertaking before the Division Bench of this Court 
in Special Appeal No. 331 of 2023 which was 
decided on 26.09.2023 that the recruitment is 
being conducted in such a way as not to disturb the 
contractual teachers.
11. He also submits that by virtue of 
an undertaking, as given before the Division Bench 
of this Court, these petitioners, who were engaged 
on contractual basis, cannot be discontinued by  virtue of the impugned order. 
12. In response to this, Mr. Arvind 
Vashisth, learned Senior Counsel submits that 
discontinuation of these contractual employees,
who are the petitioners in WPSS Nos. 909/2024, 
911/2024 and 950/2024 were not discontinued 
because of the regular selection process, rather 
they were discontinued by virtue of the terms and 
conditions of their contract and their contractual 
period was already expired. 
13. Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned counsel, 
who appears for respondent Nos. 4 & 5 submits 
that the petitioners of WPSS Nos. 909/2024, 
911/2024 and 950/2024 have no right to continue 
since they are contractual employees and they are 
bound by the terms and conditions of their 
contractual employment. Apart from this, he also 
submits that all the petitioners of these three 
petitions have also participated in the selection 
process, therefore, they cannot challenge the 
regular selection process.
14. In the meantime, two writ 
petitions have been filed i.e. WPSS No. 1945 of 
2024 and WPSS No. 1946 of 2024 by those who 
participated in the regular selection process,
initiated pursuant to an advertisement dated 
05.07.2023 and got selected and the appointment  letters have been issued. In these two subsequent 
petitions, a relief has been sought that the 
direction be issued to the respondents to give 
joining to each of the petitioners in “Eklavya Model 
Residential Schools (EMRS). 
15. Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned 
Senior Counsel, submits that because of the interim 
order passed by the coordinate Bench of this Court 
in WPSS Nos. 909/2024, 911/2024 and 950/2024 
dated 12.06.2024, the respondents are not 
permitting them to join though they are regularly 
selected, who participated in the selection process 
and by virtue of interim order passed by the 
coordinate Bench of this Court, their legitimate 
right to hold the post pursuant to their selection 
has been taken away though they were not 
impleaded as party respondents in these petitions.
16. He also submits that the 
petitions, filed by the contractual employees i.e. 
WPSS Nos. 909/2024, 911/2024 and 950 of 2024 
are liable to be dismissed also on that ground that 
they have not been impleaded the selected 
candidate as party respondent.
17. Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned 
Senior Counsel, who appears for the National 
Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS), 
informs to this Court that there are 4 Institutions, in the State of Uttarakhand, and total sanctioning 
posts are 52 for each of the Institution, and today, 
there are total 13 petitioners before this Court in 
two petitions i.e. WPSS No. 1945 of 2024 and WPSS 
No. 1946 of 2024, who are regularly selected 
candidates and have been issued appointment 
letter. He also submits that there are in total 17 
numbers of contractual employees, who are before 
this Court in three writ petitions i.e. WPSS Nos. 
909/2024, 911/2024 and 950/2024, therefore, for 
an interim measure, the petitioners of writ 
petitions i.e. WPSS No. 1945 of 2024 and WPSS No. 
1946 of 2024 may be permitted to join. 
18. He further submits that since the 
matter is being posted for final disposal, therefore, 
till such time the matter is decided finally, the 
contractual employees, who are the petitioners in 
WPSS No. 909 of 2024, WPSS No. 911/2024 and 
WPSS No. 950 of 2024, may also be permitted to 
continue.
19. Admittedly, as on today, there 
are 17 contractual employees and 13 regular 
incumbents, who are before this Court. In such an 
eventuality, the respondents are directed to give 
joining to each of the petitioner of WPSS No. 1945 
of 2024 and WPSS No. 1946 of 2024 forthwith. 
Simultaneously, the respondents are also directed  not to discontinue 17 contractual employees, who 
are before this Court in WPSS No. 909 of 2024, 911 
of 2024 and 950 of 2024 and be paid salary;
however, their continuation will be subject to the 
outcome of all these petitions.
20. Put up these matters on 
12.11.2024 as a first case along with WPSS No. 
1427 of 2023 and WPSS No. 1680 of 2023. 
21. On that day, the matter shall not 
be adjourned.
22. Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned 
Senior Counsel for the NESTS as well as Mr. C.S. 
Rawat, learned counsel for respondent Nos. 4 & 5, 
shall communicate about this order to the 
respondents for necessary compliance 
telephonically today itself.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

The Court made the following: 
COMMON ORDER:(per Hon’ble Justice Sri Rakesh Thapliyal)
 In all these writ petitions, a common issue 
has been raised whether respondent no.1- National 
Education Society for Tribal Students (for short 
“NESTS”) is authorized and competent to initiate the 
selection process to fill up the posts of Post Graduate 
Teachers (PGT) and Trained Graduate Teachers (TGT). 
2. Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned Senior Counsel, 
first of all, refer the guidelines issued by the Ministry of 
Tribal Affairs, Government of India in June, 2010, and 
particularly, he is referring Clauses 4(h) and 4(i), which 
are being reproduced here-in-below:- 
“4. Management and Running of EMRS 
(h) The tasks of school admission, appointment of 
teachers, appointment of staff, personnel matters and 
day-to-day running of the schools would be handled 
entirely by the society chosen by the State 
Government/ UT Administration and in the manner 
deemed most suitable. 
(i) The State Government/ UT Administration shall  3 
ensure and maintain the highest quality in the selection 
of teachers and staff for academic and extra-curricular 
excellence.” 
3. By referring Clauses 4(h) and 4(i) of the 
aforesaid guidelines, Mr. Bahuguna submits that the 
task of school admissions, including appointment of 
teachers, appointment of staff, would be handled 
entirely by the society chosen by the State 
Government/ UT Administration. 
4. The next document, which Mr. Bahuguna is 
referring, is the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), 
dated 26th August, 2020, which was entered into 
between NESTS and EMRS Society of the Uttarakhand 
State, which is the society established by the State. 
Clause 4 of the MoU pertains to role and responsibilities 
of the second party, i.e. EMRS Society. The second 
party in this MoU is the State Society (EMRS Society). 
Mr. Bahuguna placed reliance to Clause 4.4 and 4.5 
which are being reproduced here-in-below:- 
“4.4 Shall ensure recruitment of Teaching & Non￾Teaching Staff for the schools based on the norms and 
guidelines prescribed by Ministry of Tribal Affairs, 
Government of India from time to time in a time bound 
manner. 
4.5 Shall ensure adherence to the reservation 
policy as applicable to the sub-groups within ST 
communities, if any, in the respective State/ UT during 
the recruitment and admission process in the schools in 
consonance with the extant guidelines of the Ministry of  4 
Tribal Affairs, Government of India.” 
5. Thereafter another guidelines were issued on 
13th November, 2020, which is annexed as Annexure-17 
to the writ petition. Clause 9 of the said guidelines 
relates to running of schools. Clause 9.3(e) and (f) of 
these guidelines are relevant, and are being extracted 
here-in-below:- 
“9.3 Roles and Responsibilities of the State/ UT EMRS 
Society 
“e) Shall ensure recruitment of Teaching & Non￾Teaching Staff for the schools based on the norms and 
guidelines prescribed by Ministry of Tribal Affairs, 
Government of India from time to time in a time bound 
manner. 
f) Shall ensure adherence to the reservation policy 
as applicable to the sub-groups within ST communities, 
if any, in the respective State/ UT during the 
recruitment and admission process in the schools in 
consonance with the extant guidelines of the Ministry.” 
6. Mr. Bahuguna, by referring these Guidelines 
issued in June, 2010 and the Guidelines dated 
13.11.2020, submits that even as per these Guidelines, 
only the Society established by the State is competent 
for initiating and concluding the selection process. 
7. Apart from this, learned Senior Counsel also 
placing reliance on the letter dated 12.02.2020, issued 
by the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs,  5 
Government of India, which is addressed to the 
Principal Secretaries, Tribal Welfare Development/ 
Department of the concerned State, which contains the 
reference of statutory rules for recruitment of Teaching 
and Non-Teaching positions, which is also being 
extracted here-in-below:- 
“Dear Sir/ Madam, 
This has reference to the letter no. F. 
No.18015/1/2017- Grants dated 06.12.2019 wherein 
the comments from the States were requested on draft 
recruitment rules for Teaching and Non-Teaching Staff 
under EMRS. The last date of receiving the comments 
was 19th December 2019. 
2. After considering the comments received from 
various State Governments, the recruitment rules for 
Teaching and Non-Teaching Staff under EMRS have 
been finalized and attached at Annex-I. You are 
requested to adopt these Recruitment rules for Teaching 
and Non-teaching positions while recruitment of Staff 
under Eklavya Model Residential Schools. It is clarified 
that the State Government have to carry out the 
recruitment process for filling up various 
vacancies across the EMRSs of their States by 
following these RRs only. 
You are requested to take necessary action 
accordingly.” 
8. Mr. Bahuguna, by referring the aforesaid 
letter dated 12.02.2020, submits that even as per this 
letter, which given the reference of recruitment rules 
clearly stipulates that the Societies established by the 
State Government have to carry out the recruitment 
process for filling up various vacancies across the  6 
EMRSs of their respective States. 
9. Mr. Bahuguna submits that in view of the 
guidelines of 2010 and 2020 as well as from the 
contents of the recruitment rules, it is very clear that 
only the State Society is competent for initiating the 
selection process, and not the NESTS. 
10. Apart from this, Mr. Bahuguna submits that 
all the petitioners of this bunch of writ petitions were 
appointed, though on contractual basis, but by way of 
rigid and regular selection process by the State Society. 
In support of this argument, he has drawn the attention 
of this Court to the advertisement as well as the 
Minutes of the Selection Committee, which is appended 
as Annexure-5. Writ Petition (S/S) Nos.1945 of 2024 
and 1946 of 2024 have been preferred by those who 
have been selected pursuant to the selection process 
initiated by the NESTS.

Committee constituted for appointment of petitioners

 On the previous date, Mr. C.D. Bahuguna

recruitment would be handled entirely by the society

support his argument, he placed reliance on the

2. Today, learned Attorney General of India 
appearing for the National Education Society for Tribal 
Students (for short “NESTS”) has argued that the 
petitioners in these bunch of petitions (except in WPSS 
Nos.1945 of 2024 and 1946 of 2024) have no locus to

General gives reference of different clauses of the 
Guidelines issued on 13.11.2020, particularly, Clause 9

which deals with ‘Roles and Responsibilities of the 
National Education Society for Tribal Students, i.e. 
NESTS’, and submits that as per sub-clause k of Clause 
9.1, process of recruitment was never been entrusted 
to any other body, and it is always remained with the 
NESTS. Sub-clauses i, k, l, m and n of Clause 9.1 are 
being extracted here-in-below:- 
 “9. Running of Schools 
xxxxxx 
i) Shall provide detailed standards and norms for 
recruitment of Teaching and Non-Teaching Staff and 
continuation of existing staff. 
k) If need be, could entrust the recruitment of teachers 
for States to an independent agency duly ensuring 
reservation quota prescribed therein. 
l) Aid, establish and conduct other institutions as may 
be required for the furtherance of the Society’s  4 
objectives in any part of India. 
m. Do all such things as may be considered necessary,

EMRS Society, and by referring sub-clause (e) of Clause 
9.3, learned Attorney General submits that the 
recruitment of Teaching & Non-Teaching Staff should be 
based on the norms, guidelines and Recruitment Rules 
prescribed by the Ministry from time to time, and in 
any manner, this clause does not empower the State to 
carry on with the recruitment process through a society 
established by the State. 
5. Learned Attorney General further submits 
that on plain reading of Clause 9.1(k) with sub-clause 
(e) of Clause 9.3 of the Guidelines of 2020, since the 
recruitment process was never been entrusted to the 
State to carry on through a society established by the 
State, therefore, NESTS is the only competent body to 
go with the recruitment process. Another document, 
which has been placed by learned Attorney General, is

entered with regard to the recruitment of teachers and 
support staff for Eklavya schools sanctioned by the 
Ministry. Clause 3 of the said MoU deals with ‘Roles and 
responsibilities of the First Party as well as Second 
Party’, and the same is being extracted here-in-below:- 
“3. Roles and Responsibilities of the First Party 
Plan, construct, establish and administer the schools and to 
do all acts and things necessary for management and  6 
administration of these schools. 
Provide good quality modern education for all round 
development of students. 
Offer a common core-curriculum of NCERT to ensure

AT NAINITAL
 Writ Petition (SS) No. 1414 of 2023

and others. ………………… Petitioners.
 Versus

and others. ……………Respondents.
Present:
Mr. C. D. Bahuguna and Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, learned Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. N.K. Adhikari, 
Mr. Shubhang Dobhal and Mr. Mehul Joshi, counsel for the petitioners.
Mr. R. Venkataramani, learned Attorney General (through V.C.) with Mr. Arvind Vashisht, learned 
Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Y.C. Brijwasi, learned counsel for the NESTS.
Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned counsel for the respondents no. 3 and 5.
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. On the previous date, Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned counsel 
for the petitioners argued at length in order to give response to 
the arguments, as advanced by learned Attorney General of India 
on 11.12.2024. By referring Clause 9.3 of 2020 Guidelines issued 
by Ministry of Tribal Affair, he submits that only the State/EMRS 
society is empowered to ensure recruitment of Teaching and 
Non-Teaching staff for the schools, based on the norms, 
guidelines and the recruitment rules prescribed by the Ministry 
from time to time. On that date i.e. 05.05.2025, Mr. C.D. 
Bahuguna, learned Sr. Advocate pointed out that MoU entered 
on 22.08.2023 in between NESTS and EMRS Society is contrary to 
the 2020 Guidelines, which does not empower the NESTS to go 
with recruitment process. Furthermore, the Guidelines does not 
empower the NESTS to enter with the MoU with EMRS Society. 
He also submits that NESTS entered into MoU with ulterior 
purposes and motive. He has further placed reliance on the D.O. 
letter dated 12.02.2020 whereby all the Principal Secretaries of  2
Tribal Welfare / Development Department of each of the State 
directed to carry out the recruitment for filling up various 
vacancies. 
2. Today, Mr. R. Ventakaramani, learned Attorney General of 
India for NESTS, argued at length, in order to give response to 
the arguments, as advanced by Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned 
counsel for the petitioner. He argued that Constitution provided 
for a comprehensive framework for the protection and 
advancement of the Tribal people. Many provisions were 
specifically provided for safeguarding interest of tribal people
and with an objective of providing more focused approach on the 
integrated socio-economic development of the Scheduled Tribes, 
the most underprivileged of the Indian society, in a coordinated 
and planned manner, Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) was set 
up in the year 1999.
3. Since its inception, endeavor of Ministry of Tribal Affairs 
were to take various initiatives for overall upliftment of Tribals 
across the country. Amongst these objectives, providing quality 
education to ST students have been among the main focus of the 
Ministry as educational development is a stepping-stone to 
economic and social development and is also the most effective 
instrument for overall empowerment. 
4. He further submits that for establishing quality residential 
schools for the promotion of education and also to ensure all 
round development of tribal students in all areas, the Eklavya 
Model Residential Schools (EMRS), Eklavya Model Day Boarding 
Schools (EMDBS) and Centre of Excellence for Sports were 
established and these schools are aimed to provide quality upper 
primary, secondary and senior secondary level education to tribal 
students in tribal dominated areas, along with extra-curricular  3
activities, to enable them to access the best opportunities in 
education and to bring them at par with the general population. 
5. He also brings to the notice of this Court the revised 
Guidelines for setting up Eklavya Model Residential Schools 
(EMRS) issued by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of 
India, in June 2010 and Clause 4 of this Guidelines pertains to 
Management and running of EMRS and Clause 7 (e) provides for 
review and monitoring. It provides that the Government of India 
is free to make any modification in the aforesaid conditions in 
consultation with selected State Government / UTs whenever 
deemed necessary. Clause 7 of the said revised Guidelines is 
extracted hereinbelow:
 “Clause 7. Review and Monitoring:
a. The progress of implementation of the scheme will be 
reviewed by the Union Ministry of Tribal Affairs through 
periodic reports from the State Government/implementing 
agencies. 
b. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs will conduct review 
meetings during which States/UTs would be required to 
make presentations on the progress of their EMRSs. 
c. The guidelines for the use of the grants under Article 275 
(1) provide for an amount up to 2% of the total allocation 
to be used for administration of the programme. This would 
be applicable in case of EMRS. 
d. A Centralized mechanism for the online monitoring of the 
EMRSs would be developed. Meanwhile States/UTs may 
strength their own systems/methods.  4
e. The Government of India is free to make any modification 
in the aforesaid conditions in consultation with selected 
State Governments/UTs whenever deemed necessary.”
6. He further submits that in fact, 2010 Guidelines is past 
history and however, new Guidelines were framed by the 
Ministry on 30.11.2020 and Guidelines are applicable to all the 
schools running under EMRS Society. Clause 4 of the said 
Guidelines pertains to Management of Schools. Clause 4.1 
pertains to National Education Society for Tribal Students 
(NESTS). Clause 4.2 provides for State / UT EMRS Societies. By 
referring Clause (e) of Clause 4.2, learned Attorney General of 
India submits that Society like EMRS act as delegated authority 
by Ministry of Tribal Affairs / NESTS and not act as an 
independent authority. By referring Clause 9 of the 2020 
Guidelines, learned Attorney General of India argued that NESTS 
is empowered to review the existing MoU and to enter into fresh 
MoU and if need be, it could entrust the recruitment of teachers 
for State to an independent agency. He has particularly placed 
reliance on sub – Clause (i), (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of Clause 9.1 of 
the 2020 Guidelines. He has further placed reliance on Clause 9.3 
of the 2020 Guidelines which pertains to the Roles and 
Responsibilities of the State / UT EMRS Society, which provides 
that State/UT EMRS Societies will be responsible for the 
management of Schools sanctioned/established in the particular 
State/UT in accordance to the norms and guidelines laid down 
by the NESTS. He further submits that sub Clause (e) of Clause 
9.3 provides that EMRS Society shall ensure recruitment of 
Teaching & Non-Teaching Staff for the schools based on the 
norms, guidelines and Recruitment Rules prescribed by the 
Ministry from time to time in a time bound manner. 5
7. He further submits that NESTS is an autonomous society 
under the control of Ministry of Tribal Affairs and is empowered 
to do all the acts and things necessary for tribal education and 
NESTS will be guided by a Steering Committee headed by the
Hon’ble Minister for Tribal Affairs and as per 2020 Guidelines, 
the EMRS Society is under legal obligation to maintain, control 
and manage the Schools, as per the guidelines and norms 
formulated by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India 
and undertake other responsibilities as delegated by the Ministry 
of Tribal Affairs / NESTS. He further argued that EMRS is 
delegated authority of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and NESTS 
and since 2020 Guidelines gives comprehensive responsibility to 
the NESTS to achieve the objective for upliftment of tribal 
students and provide a detailed standards and norms for 
recruitment of Teaching and Non Teaching Staff and continuation 
of existing staff and is empowered to review the existing MoUs or 
to enter into a fresh MoU, therefore, by virtue of power conferred 
by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs under 2020 Guidelines, MoU was 
entered in between NESTS and EMRS on 22.08.2023. 
8. Apart from this, he submits that in order to maintain the 
uniformity in the standard education to tribal students, Ministry 
created NESTS and EMRS in each of the State. He further submits 
that NESTS act as a Nodal Agency of Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 
order to achieve the object under 2020 Guidelines. 
9. List on 02.06.2025 at 04.00 pm along with other connected 
petitions for further arguments.

5. Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned Senior 
Counsel for the petitioners argued that the 
National Education Society for Tribal 
Students (“for short NESTS”) is not
competent and authorized to initiate the 
selection process to fill up the post and in
reference to this, he placed reliance to 
Clause 4(h) and 4(i) of the Policy of 
Government of India of 2010. He submits 
that Policy of 2010 was further followed by 
another guidelines issued on 13.11.2020 
and as per Clause 9.3 (e) and (f), only the 
Society established by the State is 
competent to proceed with the recruitment 
process. He also submits that even by 
virtue of the Rules as framed, only the  Society established by the State is 
competent enough to carry out the 
recruitment process for filling up vacancies 
across the EMRSs of the respective States, 
therefore, the commencement of 
recruitment process by the NESTS is 
wholly without jurisdiction. In addition to 
this Mr. Bahuguna submits that as per the 
undertaking, as given before the Division 
Bench, there is a categorical assertion of 
the NESTS that the recruitment process is 
being commenced to fill up the vacancies,
which are not occupied by the petitioners,
who are appointed on contractual basis. In 
addition to this, he submits that the 
advertisement was issued by the NESTS in 
July 2023, but in order to frustrate this 
petition an MoU was entered into between 
the NESTS and EMRS Society of 
Uttarakhand on 20.08.2023, that too after 
the issuance of the advertisement and by 
this MoU, the NESTS, took the task of 
recruitment process, to fill up vacancies 
communicated by State/UT Societies. 
Finally he submits that on or before the 
said MoU dated 22.05.2023, NESTS has no 
power to carry out recruitment process.
6. On the other side Mr. R. 
Venkataramani, learned Attorney General 
submits that in respect of the selections 
carried out by the NESTS, the petitioners 
have no locus standi and furthermore the 
contractual employees, who are the 
petitioners, herein, have been 
discontinued only due to expiry of the 
period their contractual appointment.
7. Be that as it may, in view of 
statement as given before the Division 
Bench, in Special Appeal No. 331 of 2023 
that the recruitment process in question is  not being made in respect of posts held by 
the contractual employees and the NESTS 
has nothing to do with their continuation 
or discontinuation, however, the 
recruitment is being conducted in such a 
way as not to disturb the current 
contractual Teachers the interim order 
passed on 12.11.2024 is modified as 
under:-
(i) The respondents are permitted 
to appoint and give joining to the selected 
candidates, who have been declared to be 
selected pursuant to the selection process 
held by NESTS.
(ii) The petitioners, who are the 
contractual employees shall not be 
discontinued, since they are claiming their 
regularization and if they are discontinued,
it will affect their claim for regularisation.
(iii) The appointment made 
pursuant to the selection carried out by 
the NESTS and the continuation of the 
contractual Teachers shall be subject to 
the final outcome of all these petitions. 
8. Put up these matters for final 
disposal on 13.03.2026.
